questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the pedestrian, then pass them.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross, even without a marked crosswalk. Always yield to pedestrians crossing your path.

questions.question: You see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
questions.explanation: Always stop when you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog crossing. Give them plenty of space to cross safely.

questions.question: You had an argument with someone and you feel angry. What should you do?

options.text: Play loud music while driving so you do not think about it.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to calm down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. Calm down before you drive so you can focus on the road.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic will soon become one. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting.

questions.question: What do flashing arrow panels in work zones do?

options.text: Tell drivers to pull onto the shoulder and stop.
Guide drivers into correct lanes and show that part of the road is closed.
Are only used on Interstate highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Guide drivers into correct lanes and show that part of the road is closed.
questions.explanation: Flashing arrow panels guide you into the right lanes and warn you that part of the road ahead is closed. Follow all work zone signs.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect may be weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both effects may be stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with cold medicine can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: What is true about airbags in a car?

options.text: The driver does not need to wear a safety belt if the car has airbags.
Airbags work best when used with safety belts.
Children age 12 and under can safely sit in the front seat with airbags.

questions.correctAnswerText: Airbags work best when used with safety belts.
questions.explanation: Safety belts and airbags work together for better protection. Always wear your safety belt. Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat because airbags can injure them.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing red lights when it stops to pick up or drop off students. You must stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: You can go through if the intersection is clear and it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through if the intersection is clear and it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady green light allows you to continue through the intersection. Always check that the intersection is clear and yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already there.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to get there sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Stop at a safe place and rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; do not use your brakes.
Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road surface becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive only in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: This traffic sign tells drivers to travel only in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Allow extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling helps prevent accidents by letting other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Avoid staring at one thing for too long to prevent highway hypnosis. Keep your eyes moving and stay focused.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve side to side to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control of the car. Once the car is under control, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Can a driver's license be revoked for evading arrest?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Your driver license can be revoked if you try to avoid arrest or a ticket by running from a police officer.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for time to pass so your body can process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass so your body can process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to not drink and let time pass. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help keep you awake, but they do not reduce your BAC.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your car's position. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.
